A Mac for agents · optional
  Agents on every machine build, test and drive iOS simulators on one Mac: a tool, never a runner, joined from the account at its screen.
<QR>
  1. Xcode, once
     In Terminal on the Mac, in the account it joins from (yours is fine). Xcode itself comes from the App Store, and an iOS simulator runtime with xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS. Without Xcode yet, the Mac still joins: only iOS simulators wait, and its Xcode check says what to do. CocoaPods (for pod install and expo prebuild) comes from Homebrew: brew install cocoapods; its tools check gives the exact line, Homebrew's own install first where there is none.
     In Terminal on the Mac:
       # Xcode's licence and its system components, which only an admin can accept and install. Skipped while no Xcode is
       # selected yet: setup's Xcode check then says the one command that installs or selects it.
       d="$(xcode-select -p 2>/dev/null)" && test -x "$d/usr/bin/xcodebuild" && sudo xcodebuild -license accept && sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch
       # Simulators and debugging with no password prompt, for this account.
       sudo DevToolsSecurity -enable
       sudo dseditgroup -o edit -a "$(id -un)" -t user _developer
       Each line says why. It never pipes anything from the network into sudo.
<QR>
  2. Join, at the Mac's screen
     Paste the join line in Terminal on the Mac, logged in at its screen: launchd runs the node only inside that login, so su and ssh won't do. It installs fleetd for that account and joins as the agents' Mac: a tool every project's agents use, which runs no claude and no lead and takes no secret. Settings › Hub › Machines › Add machine › A Mac for agents makes the line with its one-time code; if this Mac runs fleetd already, give it that machine's name, and the line replaces it. After a restart, log that account in again: with FileVault on, macOS logs no one in by itself.
     In Terminal, logged in at the Mac's screen:
       curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh -s -- --join http://HUB --code <code> --machine-id mac --mac --version 0.0.0-edge.202611081341+e4509af
       Or on the hub: fleetd pair --worker mac, then add --mac --version 0.0.0-edge.202611081341+e4509af to the line it prints.
<QR>
  3. Two clicks at the Mac
     Turn on fleetd in Accessibility and in Screen Recording, so agents can drive the Mac's apps and you can watch them. The join opens each pane and waits for it, and the node restarts itself within seconds to take up each grant. macOS may ask for an administrator's name and password: type it in that System Settings dialog at the Mac itself, never through fleetd's view of its screen. macOS asks again from time to time; the check says when.
     Accessibility, at the Mac:
       open "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Accessibility"
       In Terminal there: it opens the pane. Turn on fleetd there.
     Screen Recording, at the Mac:
       open "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture"
       The same for Screen Recording.
<QR>
  4. A Mac that runs fleetd already
     Give the join line the name it has, in the same account, and it becomes the agents' Mac in place, keeping its history. Let the agents running there finish (or stop them) first. Joined under another name or from another account, the old machine stays until you remove it: the Mac's checks say so, and how.
     On the hub, for an old machine of another name:
       fleetd machine remove <old name>
       Where it ran in another account on the Mac, stop it there too: launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/sh.fleetd.node
<QR>
  5. Optional: a user of its own for agents
     Agents act as the account the node runs in, so they can read what it can. To keep them out of yours, make a standard user for them, log in as it at the Mac's screen, and join from there instead.
     In your own (admin) account's Terminal:
       # A standard user of its own for agents. You choose its password and keep it.
       sudo sysadminctl -addUser agents -fullName "fleetd agents" -password -
       sudo dseditgroup -o edit -a agents -t user _developer
       # Your own home closed to other users, agents included.
       chmod 700 ~
       sysadminctl asks for the new user's password, which you keep; agents never get it.
<QR>
  In the app: Settings › Hub › Machines.
<QR>
  Test: Read the Mac's checks, which its node runs every 30 seconds (its grants every 2 while one is off).
–  A Mac for agents optional · fleetd init --step mac

Run fleetd init --step mac again when you've done it; it keeps what's done.
